items.followUp: Describe the structure of the cell wall.

rubric.why: Recognises the membrane’s basic layered structure.
rubric.description: The cell membrane is made of a phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the membrane as a double layer of phospholipids.

rubric.why: Shows the orientation of both parts of the phospholipids in the bilayer.
rubric.description: The hydrophilic heads face the watery environments on either side, and the hydrophobic tails face inward toward one another.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly stating the orientation of both the heads and tails.

rubric.why: Includes proteins as structural components of the membrane and places them in the bilayer.
rubric.description: Protein molecules are embedded in the phospholipid bilayer.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying embedded membrane proteins.

rubric.why: Names the fluid mosaic model or gives a key property associated with the membrane.
rubric.description: The membrane is described by the fluid mosaic model and is selectively permeable.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming the fluid mosaic model or stating that the membrane is selectively or partially permeable.

modelAnswer: The cell membrane is a thin, flexible phospholipid bilayer with proteins embedded in it.
The hydrophilic heads of the phospholipids face outward toward the watery environments on both sides of the membrane.
The hydrophobic tails face inward toward one another.
This arrangement is described by the fluid mosaic model, and the membrane is selectively permeable.
